memos.risk:
**Risk officer call: REFUSE. No size.**

The brief shows a coin that already ran 7.1x in 30 minutes, is now 52% off its high, and is bleeding (-21% over 15 min, sell/buy ratio 0.94 in the launch window). The "ORGANIC" label doesn't hold up: bundle_share is 97.2% and top-3 curve share is 68%, so the curve is almost certainly bundled/wash-driven, not organic. The first two minutes were 398 SOL from 247 buyers, but top-5 buyers hold only 13.5%, which is consistent with a launch bot spreading volume, not a real holder base.

Pool depth (285 SOL) is thin enough that a $20 round trip at 1.4-5.1% cost is survivable, but the exit risk is the real issue. A 52% drawdown with 2,459 sellers in the last 15 minutes means exits are crowded.

The name ("Blood Fomo") is a creator-chosen hype label and gets no weight from me.

Skip. A missed coin costs nothing.
memos.scout:
The honest case for buying blofomo now is weak, and I don't think the brief supports a buy.

What looks like demand: 2,685 buyers and about $2.0M in volume over the last 15 minutes, a 7.1x return over 30 minutes, and a launch with 247 non-agent buyers in the first two minutes, with the top-5 buyer share only 13.5%.

Why it doesn't hold up: the last 15 minutes net to only 121.6 SOL against 8,623 SOL bought, with 2,459 sellers against 2,685 buyers. That is almost pure churn, and the coin is already 52% off its 30-minute high. The first two minutes show a 0.94 sell-to-buy ratio, and the curve shows a 97% bundle share, 68% of supply held by the top 3, and a completer share of 63%. Those are the signatures of a coin being rotated by its early holders, not one with fresh demand arriving. Demand that will still be here in 30-60 minutes would show net inflow, not an even split of sellers and buyers at a lower price.

Verdict: no honest case for buying now. Skip.
memos.skeptic: The most likely loss is a sharp exit by the insiders who pumped this coin. Their curve data shows bundled supply: bundle_share is 0.972, and the top3 holders control 68% of the curve. The completer holds 63%, so whoever drove the graduation can dump on us. Last 15 minutes: 8,623 SOL bought against 8,501 SOL sold, with 2,459 sellers versus 2,685 buyers, and price already down 21%. Net flow of only 121 SOL means the buyers are exhausted. Two minutes after graduation the sell-to-buy ratio was 0.94, meaning nearly every buy was matched by a sell. We're already 52% below the 30-minute high, and a $20 ticket faces 1.4-5.1% round-trip costs. Skip.
